Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collisoin in a parking lot with complaints of acute low back pain and muscle
tightness radiating into the left paraspinal region. Initial evaluation documented restricted lumbar range of motion and
localized tenderness without neurological deficit. Imaging and examination fnidings cleraly confirm a soft tissue injury
consistent with lumbar strain. Causation has not yet been firmly established, as the timing and mechanism of onset
are still being reviewed against the patient's reported history. No prior injury to the lumbar region is known from the
records available to this office. Care was delivered over twelve visits consisting of manual therapy, guided stretching,
and a home exercise program. Treatment followed a typical clinical course, with pain scores and mobility improving
steadily and visit frequency tapering as the patient recovered. Billing records reflect single entries for each service
with no repeated charges. Patient is currently discharged to self-directed exercise with instructions to return if
symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
